gap: No result ChatGPT got states that LiTime's 16 A breaker only protects the 12 V accessory sockets and that LiTime states no breaker for the trolling-motor terminals (6 AWG leads, M8 ring terminals), while the Newport and Minn Kota boxes put a 60 A breaker on the motor circuit. None of them states that Newport's own store listing calls the Smart Battery Box 'Not compatible with lithium batteries', when its FAQ blames only the LED meter.
standout_why: I compared against the pages ChatGPT cited: Minn Kota's amp-draw/breaker article, the Battery Power Center (No Longer Manufactured) page, the Minn Kota wiring guide and Newport's Smart Battery Box FAQs. I also checked Newport's Circuit Breaker Compatibility page, which ChatGPT got but did not cite. The Minn Kota pages give breaker sizing by motor and the Power Center's 60 A/10 A breakers, but they say nothing about third-party boxes. Newport's FAQ says only the LED meter fails with lithium. Newport's breaker page already lists 50 A for its 40/46/55/86 lb motors, so the point that the built-in 60 A is oversized for most of them is NOT new. ChatGPT's own answer said of LiTime 'check the motor-circuit protection rating' and left it open, so no page it got settles that the 16 A breaker covers only the accessories. Its second answer also turned the Newport lithium problem into 'indicator not accurate', which plays down the store's own wording.
decides: The 'breaker' line on these boxes means different things. On Newport and Minn Kota it is a 60 A breaker on the motor circuit. On LiTime it is a 16 A breaker on the accessory sockets only. So LiTime ($84.99 today) is not a breaker-equipped alternative to Newport ($69.99): it still needs an inline motor breaker sized to the motor. For the lead-acid shopper, Newport stays the pick, though most Newport motors under 62 lb also need Newport's recommended 50 A or 40 A breaker. For a LiFePO4 shopper, Newport's store listing rules its box out. LiTime ('suitable for Lithium') plus a separate 50–60 A breaker becomes the pick, or the discontinued Minn Kota Power Center, where Minn Kota says lithium works but the meter always shows full.
